payload.summary: Nothing compares the replayed migration chain against supabase/schema.sql, so a migration that changes a function body without a matching schema.sql edit passes every pre-merge gate and only surfaces post-merge in live-drift
payload.detail: Root-caused 2026-09-01 from live-drift run 33484535655 (red on main at d3074946a, sole finding: correct_clinical_query_terms(text,real) def_hash manifest e2356565 vs live 2ebaf978). PR #2477's migration 20260831100000 redefined that function with a duplicated 'and length(canonical) between 4 and 40' predicate; supabase/schema.sql was never updated to match, so the manifest (generated by replaying schema.sql into the pinned supabase/postgres:17.6.1.127 container) disagreed with live. CI's db-reset-verify job DOES replay migrations (supabase migration up --local) and DOES regenerate the manifest, but its only assertion is committed.schema_sha256 === generated.schema_sha256 (.github/workflows/ci.yml ~L1082-1095) — i.e. 'schema.sql did not change without a manifest refresh'. Nothing asserts the replayed chain equals schema.sql, which is the actual mirror invariant. Same failure class as the original #316 root cause (SET work_mem absent from schema.sql). Candidate fix: in db-reset-verify, after 'supabase migration up --local', dump the replayed local schema and diff its catalog snapshot against the schema.sql-derived manifest snapshot, failing the PR on any object-level divergence. Behaviour impact of this specific instance: none (duplicated predicate is a boolean no-op); the gap itself is the finding.
